newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Hollinger amends bid for Southam.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Hollinger amends bid for Southam.

text.p: Canada's Hollinger Inc. said on Wednesday it amended its bid to acquire the shares of Southam Inc. it did not already own, days after some minority Southam shareholders complained its offer was too low.

Toronto-based Hollinger, whose newspaper titles include London's Daily Telegraph, the Chicago Sun-Times and the Jerusalem Post, already owns 50.45 percent of Southam, Canada's largest newspaper chain.

Hollinger originally offered C$23.50 ($16.94) a share for the minority shares, with the bid consisting of C$13.50 ($9.72) in cash and C$10 ($7.22) in the form of a Hollinger Canadian non-voting special share.

Hollinger said on Wednesday that each Hollinger special share offered in exchange would now be denominated in U.S. instead of Canadian dollars and be exchangeable into class A Hollinger International Inc. shares over a three-year period.
The amended offer will expire on June 23.
Southam's special committee, established to consider the offer, said on Wednesday it would recommend acceptance of the amended offer to Southam's board of directors.
Trading in Southam was halted on the Toronto Stock Exchange early in Wednesday's session for the news. It last traded at C$22.55, down C15 cents.
Hollinger Inc. closed down C10 cents to C$11.60 in Toronto. Hollinger International fell 37.5 cents to $11.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Toronto-based Hollinger Inc holds 51.2 percent of the shares and 77.7 percent of the voting power of Hollinger International.
